args.shared:
CLIENT PRIORITY #1 (21 Nov 12:35, verbatim): "prio, ensure bagian ini sama kaya di design, gini yaa, color dan reflectionnya". THIS PART = the lake under the sculpture: the concentric ripple rings, the near water and its glint, down to the rocks. It must look like the design in COLOUR and REFLECTION.
TARGET: MAIN/notes/round11/refs_user/ripple_target_2026-11-21.png (the client's own crop, 1037x325 = the Figma box x325 y524 w762 h239 of the 1440x766 frame, ~1.36x, = F000's bottom centre). Also REF ref_F000.png (1x) and the Default Loop frames loop_F000..F120 (how the rings move).
ROUND 1 FAILED (lane LANES/p4rip, lab :5170 still up; read FIRST: its HANDOFF.md, and the judge's and re-judge's LOG.md in MAIN/notes/round11/lane_backup/p4pri/{p4rip,judge_p4rip,rejudge_p4rip}/; tools you may copy: $SP/work_p4/p4rip/tools and $SP/work_p4/rejudge_p4rip/tools: rj_ana.py (the target-zoom boxes and the numbers table), rj_rings.py, rj_glint.py, shoot_ripple.mjs (deterministic frames, hero frozen, same clock on two labs), shimmer.py + jblipmap.py (60 fps sparkle), the pop / crawl scripts (waterline AA)). Right in round 1: the ring = Blender's Wave crest train (z = 0.226 exp(-(2.362 a)^2), 2.717 m apart, 1.115 m/s, centre Blender (0, 8.6); Blender's front at F000 = 5.98 m); the trough colour at 1x (114,139,177 sat 0.35 = F000). WRONG in round 1 (the lead looked: the rings read as flat PAINTED bands / contour lines and the glint as a pale grey-mint smear; MAIN looks more natural): (1) flat, posterized band fills with thin light crest lines and no facet texture inside the bands; (2) the glint a smooth dim lobe (top 5 % 205,212,221) instead of granular cyan-white glitter (F000 212,228,242; cyan-white px target 3180 / F000 2210 vs lane 5-18); (3) only 2-3 visible rings at the target zoom after the front was cut to 5.3 m (target: 4-5 dark bands across the whole water); (4) waterline AA: new pop clusters on the bottom rocks' top edge, right-slab crawl +60 %; (5) its first build: white 'mercury' blobs and 3x MAIN's 60 fps sparkle.
WHAT THE TARGET SHOWS (lead's read): 4-5 wavy, slightly irregular cobalt / steel-blue trough bands with silvery crests across the whole ring field; fine facet texture (small ripples) all over the water that breaks the reflection into short strokes, INSIDE the bands too; a granular cyan-white glitter band in the MIDDLE of the rings under the sculpture (many small highlights - not a smooth lobe, not one sparkle low in the frame); the sculpture's rippled reflection near the top; light silvery-blue water between the bands; blue water with sparkle by the bottom rocks.
FACTS FROM THE ARTIST'S .blend (MAIN/hero-pipeline/research/blender_forensics.md, read the water + world + sun parts): the water is a pure mirror (Principled, Metallic 1.0, white, roughness 0.0345, no Fresnel falloff), the near water Plane.011 is a 64x64 grid (0.4647 m) + Wave + SubD L2 + Smooth by Angle with the 'Procedural Water Surface' material; glossy rays skip the BG.001 card and see the darker, more saturated Nishita world sky (sun elev 18.70 deg, rot -61.0 deg, outside the frame), the cloud cards and the geometry.
LEAD'S DIAGNOSIS OF MAIN (verify it, do not take it on faith): int3's Water.ts (~ lines 2610-2645) shades the crest bands as a LUMA-ONLY ratio on the plate: k = clamp((luma(rRip) - luma(rFlat)) / luma(rFlat) * uRippleShade, -0.48, 0.48); base *= 1 + k. A tilted facet in the .blend reflects higher, bluer, more saturated sky, so the troughs should shift in HUE toward cobalt; a luma ratio can only darken the plate's pale grey-blue (MAIN's grey bands), and pushing it harder gave 'smooth over-dark painted stripes' in QC rounds 6-7. MAIN also damps the breeze / bump grain to 0.3 inside the ring zone (~ line 2128) because it 'masked the bands', which is why the bands are smooth. The glint (orb glitter + P4 water Q8 GGX, ~ lines 1382-1430 and 2700-2730) sits lower than the target's.
ACCEPTANCE (the client's eye decides; the lead looks before anything merges): side by side TARGET | LANE | MAIN (:5179) at the target zoom (DPR 2 render of the Figma box, rejudge_p4rip's tz_ method, resized to 1037x325) and at 1x vs F000 (crop x201-1238 y441-766), at >= 3 clocks (t 100, 100.6, 101.2): at a glance the lane must read CLEARLY closer to the target than MAIN in ring visibility and contrast, trough hue, texture, glint and reflection, with nothing painted and nothing CG. If it does not, you are not done (say so honestly). Fill the rejudge's numbers table (zone mean, sdL, sat, troughs 15 %, trough sat, crests, glint crest, glint p99 L, low box, white px, cyan-white px, ring count) for TARGET / LANE / MAIN / int3.
HARD GATES (re-run every one on your FINAL build, numbers in HANDOFF): (a) your switch off == :5173 exactly (ident: final image + all targets + all programs, 20 moving frames, T1 and T2 and T0 phone, plus p04 / p06 / p07); (b) waterline AA vs :5173 with the bloom-free masks and all SIX pop paths (slow, medium, fast, diag, reverse, leave): 0 new clusters >= 6 px, per-region crawl mc32 not worse than +10 % (MAIN/notes/round11/workflows/briefs/aa8_common.md); (c) 60 fps sparkle: 40 consecutive frames at 1/60 s, hero frozen, same clock: blips |dL| > 10 per frame <= :5173's in every box (zone, glint, near, bottom rocks); (d) nothing outside the lake changes (region means == :5173 for sky, mountains, iceberg, floes, rocks, hero box within run-to-run noise); the ice rings' look unchanged; (e) perf: T1 real loop, rest AND pointer-sweep modes, >= 6 VALID interleaved pairs at load < 10 (SLOT_BG=0 STRICT=1, int2's perfab.mjs), <= +5 % vs :5173; (f) the hold / release poses p04-p08 not worse than :5173 (the hold bottom strip is w4's work: keep it); (g) tsc clean (both configs); 0 console errors.

explorers.approach: APPROACH A - 'MAIN up': start from int3's (= MAIN's) ripple shading, which the lead and the round-1 re-judge find more natural, and move it to the target step by step, measuring each step against the target zoom and F000 (keep a dated table in LOG). Levers, in the order the lead expects them to matter: (1) the trough hue: replace the luma-only crest ratio with the reflected sky's COLOUR (e.g. a per-channel ratio rRip / rFlat, or a mix toward the reflected radiance at the tilted normal) so troughs turn cobalt / steel-blue and crests silvery, symmetric so the bands average to the calm plate (F000's zone mean 157,174,198 at the target zoom); check first what uEnvMap holds for the reflected directions (is it the Nishita world's darker, saturated sky the .blend's glossy rays see?); (2) the ring count / extent: Blender's front 5.98 m with a feather that keeps the left slab calm (F000 is calm left of x ~420 on rows 575-600); (3) the texture inside the bands: let the bump / breeze facets (or w4's band-limited mipmapped lake_chop.png normals, already in int3) show inside the ring zone so the reflection breaks into short strokes, without masking the bands; (4) the glint: move MAIN's granular glitter up into the middle of the rings (compute where the orb's / the sun's mirror point falls; compare with the target's glint position), tint it cyan-white BEFORE the tone map so it does not clip to white, band-limited by the mipmapped normals so it does not sparkle at 60 fps. Switch: ?p4rxa=0 restores :5173 exactly.
explorers.label: explore:rxa

explorers.approach: APPROACH B - 'Cycles ground truth': first render the artist's scene in Cycles to learn what makes the target's look, then make the engine reproduce each component. (1) Blender 5.2 (Metal) on a COPY of the artist's scene: MAIN/blender/'Home - EXPORT.zip' (unzip into your WORK; never save over any .blend in the repo; one Blender at a time machine-wide, through the slot), the camera = the engine's REST_CAMERA (app/hero/engine/config.ts; earlier rounds matched it to F000: MAIN/notes/round11/handoff_env.md and the bake scripts under MAIN/blender/ show how) at F000's moment (the Wave modifier's frame for Loop F000; forensics), a border render of the Figma box (x325 y524 w762 h239 of 1440x766) at 2x, enough samples for a clean image, plus passes: Glossy Direct / Glossy Indirect / Emission / Normal, and variants 'Wave off' and 'bump off' (the Procedural Water Surface material's bump at 0). Time-box Blender to 40 min; if the scene will not render, say so and work with what you have. PUBLISH the renders as soon as they exist to $SP/work_p4/rip2_gt/ with a README (camera, frame, samples, what each file is) - the other explorer may use them. (2) Decompose: which component makes the troughs' cobalt, the crests, the facet texture and the granular glitter (the sun? the orb? the sky?), and where the glint sits. (3) In the engine (start from int3's Water.ts), reproduce each component against its pass (the ring's normal into the reflection lookups / env radiance with the right sky, the bump's facets, the glint from the right light with a filtered, band-limited lobe), checking each against its pass and the target zoom. Switch: ?p4rxb=0 restores :5173 exactly.
explorers.label: explore:rxb

args.pick: ROLE: independent PICK JUDGE of the ripple round 2 (read-only: never edit a lane; labs :5175 = explorer A 'MAIN up', :5176 = explorer B 'Cycles ground truth', :5173 = int3_base, :5179 = MAIN). Folder $SP/work_p4/pick_rip2; mirror to MAIN/notes/round11/lane_backup/p4pri2/pick/. Make your OWN deterministic captures (hero frozen, same clocks t 100, 100.6, 101.2 on all four labs; the target-zoom DPR 2 Figma box and 1x) and sheets TARGET | A | B | MAIN at the target zoom and at 1x vs F000 (also 2x crops of the glint and of a trough band), and the numbers table for TARGET / A / B / MAIN. Then check the hard gates each explorer reports, re-running the cheapest decisive ones yourself (ident of the switch at T1; 60 fps sparkle on the glint box; one fast pop path). Decide: winner = the explorer that reads clearly closer to the target than MAIN at a glance AND whose open gate failures look fixable in 90 min; or 'none' if neither beats MAIN clearly. List exactly what the winner must still fix, and any part of the loser worth grafting (only if small and gate-safe, with file / lines).
args.finish: ROLE: FINISHER of the ripple round 2 in the WINNING lane (you own its lab now). Apply the pick judge's must-fix list and any listed graft; then make EVERY hard gate pass on the final build (re-run all of them; numbers in HANDOFF); produce the client sheets TARGET | LANE | MAIN at the target zoom and at 1x vs F000 at three clocks, plus a 2x glint crop, saved also to MAIN/notes/round11/refs_user/rip2_*.jpg; refresh the full capture set (qc_r11.zsh) into WORK/qc_final; the patch vs int3_base (LANES/int3_base/retrux-web/app); HANDOFF.md (files + hunks, switches, numbers, what is still different from the target). If a part cannot pass its gates, take it out (or put it behind an opt-in switch) rather than ship it. Leave the lab running.
args.judge: LENSES to score: environment, color_grade_post, awwwards_jury, glitch_hold_sweep. The client's question decides: does the ripple area now look like the client's target (MAIN/notes/round11/refs_user/ripple_target_2026-11-21.png) and F000 - colour (troughs, crests, water tone), the ring pattern, the facet texture, the glint band, the reflection - and clearly more than MAIN (:5179)? Side by side target | lane | MAIN at the target zoom and at 1x / 2x; the numbers; 60 fps sparkle; all six pop paths and the crawl regions; nothing else in the frame changed; the hold / release poses.
